newsitem.title: GERMANY: Big police search near Frankfurt for kidnap victim.
newsitem.headline: Big police search near Frankfurt for kidnap victim.

text.p: German police launched a big search in countryside east of Frankfurt on Thursday in their efforts to find kidnapped multi-millionaire Jakub Fiszman, who disappeared on October 1.

About 500 police with sniffer dogs were involved in the operation in woods and fields in the Taunus area, about 50 km (30 miles) from the German financial centre, a spokesman for the regional criminal investigations office in Wiesbaden said.

Police sealed off several hectares (acres) of land and barred the scores of journalists and television camera crews from entering the area in case they destroyed vital clues pointing to the whereabouts of the 40-year-old businessman.
"It is possible that he's still alive," a police spokesman at the scene told reporters.

German police recovered four million marks ($2.6 million) in ransom money paid to the Fiszmann's kidnappers and have arrested three German men and two women they believed to be the main suspects on Wednesday.

The suspects, who were aged between 26 and 51 years, had in part confessed to the crime, prosecutor Reiner Schilling told a news conference on Tuesday. One of the women had worked in Fiszmann's property firm for 10 years.
The ransom money was found in the garden of a flat in Wiesbaden, with two 1,000 mark notes ($650) missing.
Authorities said previously they believed Fiszmann was still alive even though the kidnappers had reneged on a promise to free him after the ransom was paid last week.

Fiszmann, a member of one of Germany's richest families, was abducted outside his Frankfurt office. The only contact with Fiszmann in the intervening 17 days has been one phone call he made to a contact, believed to be his girlfriend, saying he was being kept in a cellar.
Fiszmann's brother Georg paid the ransom on October 10, but his kidnappers failed to free him as promised the following day.
